item.title: Deepal rolls into Fiji as demand for electric vehicles grows
item.description: Fijians looking at making the switch to electric vehicles now have more options, with the Tappoo Group officially launching Deepal in Fiji The launch was held at Carcity in Nadi and was attended by corporate customers, media representatives and a visiting Deepal delegation .
item.content:encoded:
Fijians looking at making the switch to electric vehicles now have more options, with the Tappoo Group officially launching Deepal in Fiji

The launch was held at Carcity in Nadi and was attended by corporate customers, media representatives and a visiting Deepal delegation .

Three models were unveiled - the S05, available in fully electric and range extended variants , the S07 , a premium electric vehicle , and the hunter K50,a range extended electric pickup .

Tappoo Group's Ravi Tappoo says the company would focus on providing reliable after-sales support, spare parts and trained technicians for Deepal customers.

The group also confirmed plans to establish a dedicated Deepal showroom in Suva, saying the investment reflects its confidence in the future of the electric mobility in Fiji.

Deepal vehicles are now on display at Carcity in Nadi.

item.title: M-PAiSA operator Digital Financial Services named PayTech of the Year finalist at Asia Fintech Awards
item.description: Digital Financial Services Pte Limited (DFS), the operator of Fiji's leading mobile money platform M-PAiSA, has been named a finalist in the highly coveted PayTech of the Year category at the Asia Fintech Awards 2026. The Asia Fintech Awards recognise excellence, innovation, and impact among the region's leading financial technology providers.
item.content:encoded:
Digital Financial Services Pte Limited (DFS), the operator of Fiji's leading mobile money platform M-PAiSA, has been named a finalist in the highly coveted PayTech of the Year category at the Asia Fintech Awards 2026.

The Asia Fintech Awards recognise excellence, innovation, and impact among the region's leading financial technology providers.

General Manager Digital Financial Services, Shailendra Prasad says being selected as a finalist is a significant achievement for Fiji and a testament to the impact M-PAiSA has made in transforming financial services across the country.

Prasad says it is a proud moment for the team, with the awards attracting submissions from some of the most innovative and highly regarded fintech companies across the region .

He says for M-PAiSA to be recognised as a finalist among such distinguished industry peers is both commendable and a tremendous honour.

Prasad says the nomination demonstrates that a home-grown Fijian digital wallet platform can successfully compete shoulder-to-shoulder with some of Asia's largest and most sophisticated financial technology providers.

He says the recognition validates DFS's vision, investment in innovation, and commitment to delivering accessible financial services to all Fijians.

He says since its launch, M-PAiSA has played a pivotal role in advancing financial inclusion throughout Fiji by providing convenient, secure, and affordable digital financial services to individuals, businesses, and communities across the country.

Prasad says the platform's contribution extends beyond digital payments, helping to create meaningful social and economic impact.

He says DFS is proud that its efforts to improve access to financial services and drive economic participation have been recognised on such a prominent and prestigious regional platform.

He says the nomination reflects DFS's ongoing efforts to expand the digital payments ecosystem in Fiji through innovative solutions that enable customers to transact, save time, and participate more fully in the digital economy.

Prasad says DFS is honoured by the recognition and grateful to its customers, partners and stakeholders who have supported its journey.

He says while being named a finalist is already a significant achievement, the company remains hopeful of securing the ultimate award and bringing the prestigious recognition home to Fiji.

The winners will be announced at a gala awards ceremony to be held in Singapore on 21st August.

item.title: TOPEX to remain at Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa for next two years
item.description: Great news as Fiji’s business community will continue to have a platform to connect, discuss economic opportunities and build partnerships, with the Top Executive Conference (TOPEX) set to remain at Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa for the next two years. The Fiji Commerce and Employers Federation (FCEF) says they have renewed its partnership with Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa as the official venue partner f
item.content:encoded:
Great news as Fiji’s business community will continue to have a platform to connect, discuss economic opportunities and build partnerships, with the Top Executive Conference (TOPEX) set to remain at Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa for the next two years.

The Fiji Commerce and Employers Federation (FCEF) says they have renewed its partnership with Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa as the official venue partner for TOPEX 2026 and TOPEX 2027.

They say TOPEX is recognised as one of Fiji’s leading business events, bringing together business leaders, investors, policymakers, development partners and industry representatives to discuss issues shaping the country’s economic future.

TOPEX Committee Chair and FCEF Vice President Rowena Taito says the renewed partnership will strengthen FCEF’s ability to deliver a quality conference experience for delegates, sponsors and partners.

Taito says TOPEX provides an opportunity for Fiji’s business leaders to gain new perspectives, build networks and take practical ideas back into their organisations.

She says having a trusted venue partner allows FCEF to focus on creating a programme that provides value to participants.

Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa Director of Sales Michael Bell says the partnership reflects the resort’s commitment to supporting Fiji’s business community.

Bell says TOPEX provides an opportunity to support a high-level business gathering that encourages collaboration, strengthens networks and contributes to the continued growth of Fiji’s private sector.

TOPEX 2026 will be held from 19th to 21st November at Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa in Denarau.

Registrations are now open, with participant numbers limited to maintain the quality of engagement and overall conference experience.

For registration you can visit their website www.fcef.com.fj.

item.title: PM says BSP Life driving jobs and investment while company donates $150,000 to Wellness Coalition
item.description: As BSP Life celebrates it 150th Anniversary, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says investments by the organisation directly translate into employment opportunities, capacity building for local communities, and sustainable economic returns for resource owners and ensure that tangible benefits are meaningfully shared across communities, villages, and families throughout Fiji, creating a living legacy
item.content:encoded:
As BSP Life celebrates it 150th Anniversary, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says investments by the organisation directly translate into employment opportunities, capacity building for local communities, and sustainable economic returns for resource owners and ensure that tangible benefits are meaningfully shared across communities, villages, and families throughout Fiji, creating a living legacy of opportunity for future generations.

While speaking during the celebration at the Grand Pacific Hotel, Rabuka highlights that through the Yavu Collective and in partnership with Fiji Airways, they will open three new hotels over the next six months to complement its Sofitel asset on Denarau Island.

He also says a partnership with Dubai-based Kerzner International is planned to develop an ultra-luxury resort on Nacula Island in the Yasawas by 2029.

Rabuka says these developments will collectively elevate Fiji's position as a regional hub in the Pacific, further strengthening our tourism outlook on the international platform.

He says during peak periods, these major investments by BSP Life ensure that we have the world-class accommodation to meet growing demands and drive long-term economic growth.

Rabuka further says BSP Life's long-standing commitment to promoting financial security and long-term financial planning contribute directly to the national objectives of building a more inclusive, resilient, and financially empowered society.

The Prime Minister says by encouraging households to save, to invest, and plan for the future, the institution supports greater economic resilience at both the family and national levels.

He says as the nation's second-largest institutional investor after the Fiji National Provident Fund, the organisation plays a critical role in mobilising domestic savings and directing capital towards productive investments.

He says these investments support enterprise development, infrastructure, employment creation and broader economic activity, all of which are essential if Fiji is to achieve the sustained growth needed to realise its ambition of becoming a high-income economy by 2050.

Rabuka adds the government remains committed to working closely with responsible institutions such as BSP Life in advancing the priorities of the National Development Plan, expanding financial inclusion, strengthening economic resilience, promoting healthier communities, and increasing investment in the sectors that will drive sustainable growth.

BSP Life Group CEO Mark Robinson says they serve millions of customers through banking and insurance, united by a common purpose of championing prosperity for the South Pacific.

He says they recognize that the financial services landscape continues to evolve very rapidly, driven by changing customer expectations, emerging technologies and new market dynamics, both in Fiji, around the region and across the globe, customers expect greater convenience, more personalized services and sustainable value.

Robinson says BSP Life is investing in technology, strengthening its capabilities, optimising its group strengths and building for the future, while remaining true to the values that have earned the trust of generations of Fijians.

He says while technology continues to evolve, trust remains timeless.

Robinson says although the company is proud of its history, it is now entering the next chapter of its journey. He says the world ahead will be vastly different from the one it inherited, bringing new opportunities and challenges as a new generation of customers looks to institutions like BSP Life to help them achieve their aspirations.

Robinson also thanked BSP Life's customers across Fiji for their loyalty, saying many families have chosen the company for generations.

As part of their anniversary celebrations, BSP Life launched the Healthy Choices BSP Life Corporate Wellness Program and donated $150,000 to the Wellness Coalition to support its work in promoting healthy lifestyles across Fiji.

item.title: Dulux launches two new sustainable products as it marks 40 years in Fiji
item.description: Two new innovative products aimed at supporting environmentally responsible and sustainable building practices has been launched by Dulux as the company marks 40 years of its brand presence in Fiji. Dulux says the new products reflect its continued focus on innovation and sustainability as it celebrates four decades of providing paint solutions for homes, businesses and communities across Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Two new innovative products aimed at supporting environmentally responsible and sustainable building practices has been launched by Dulux as the company marks 40 years of its brand presence in Fiji.

Dulux says the new products reflect its continued focus on innovation and sustainability as it celebrates four decades of providing paint solutions for homes, businesses and communities across Fiji.

Today, Pacific Coatings says it has grown into one of the region’s leading manufacturers, operating two manufacturing facilities, four warehouses and six trade centres while employing more than 100 people.

The anniversary milestone was marked through corporate events at the Grand Pacific Hotel and Crowne Plaza, bringing together customers, business partners, employees and industry stakeholders to reflect on the company’s journey and future plans.

Dulux says while the Dulux brand was introduced to Fiji in 1986, its roots go back to 1968 when British Paints established Fiji’s first paint manufacturing facility, becoming the country’s pioneering paint manufacturer and laying the foundation for the local industry.

The company says a major turning point came in 1986 when ICI Paints acquired British Paints and introduced the globally recognised Dulux brand to the Fijian market.

The company says a new chapter began in 2006 when Pacific Coatings Pte Limited, led by local shareholders Viliame Leqa, Greg Lawlor and Neil Underhill, acquired the business, marking the beginning of a period focused on local ownership, investment and regional expansion .

Dulux says through a strategic supply, trade and technology partnership with Dulux Group Australia, Pacific Coatings has continued to strengthen its manufacturing capability while introducing world-class products and technologies to the Pacific market.

The company says it supplies products to more than eight Pacific Island countries, supporting thousands of customers across the region.

The company says further expansion is underway, with Pacific Coatings acquiring strategic commercial properties in Suva and progressing plans for a new purpose-built manufacturing facility in Lami.

Dulux says the new facility is expected to increase production capacity, improve operational efficiency and create new employment opportunities while supporting the company’s long-term growth strategy.

Speaking on the milestone, Pacific Coatings CEO Roshan Singh says the anniversary represents more than four decades of business success.

Singh says the journey from British Paints to Dulux has been built on innovation, resilience and strong partnerships.

He says the company is proud to be a 100 percent locally owned company that continues to invest in Fiji, its people and the wider Pacific.

Singh says the anniversary celebrates past achievements while reaffirming the company’s commitment to delivering quality products and sustainable solutions for generations to come.

item.title: Customary fishing rights owners to receive 80% of royalties under new regulations
item.description: Owners of customary fishing rights will now receive 80 percent of royalties collected when certain natural resources are extracted from State land in areas linked to their customary fishing rights. A People’s Alliance Party statement says under new regulations introduced by Minister for Lands and Mineral Resources Filimoni Vosarogo, the remaining 20 percent of the royalties will go to the State.
item.content:encoded:
Owners of customary fishing rights will now receive 80 percent of royalties collected when certain natural resources are extracted from State land in areas linked to their customary fishing rights.

A People’s Alliance Party statement says under new regulations introduced by Minister for Lands and Mineral Resources Filimoni Vosarogo, the remaining 20 percent of the royalties will go to the State.

This means that when resources such as sand, gravel, clay, soil, rock, top soil and river spalls are extracted, the owners of customary fishing rights will receive the larger share of the royalty payments.

The new royalty rate for sand and gravel is $10.40 per cubic metre, while clay and soil are set at $6.50 per cubic metre.

The rate for rock is $5.21 per cubic metre, top soil is $38.99 per cubic metre and river spalls are $7.80 per cubic metre.

Sand extracted from drainage and irrigation dump sites will attract a royalty rate of $8 per cubic metre.

The regulations also require these royalty rates to be reviewed every five years to ensure they remain fair and reflect market conditions.

The People’s Alliance Party says the move is aimed at ensuring iTaukei resource owners receive a fairer share of the benefits from Fiji’s natural resources.

It says Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka and the party believe that people who have protected these resources for generations should receive a fair return from their use.

The party says the new regulations will help strengthen communities and ensure development provides direct benefits to resource owners.
